A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same post-pruning scaling-law study, with readable text, equations, tables and figures. V1 ends after its references; v2 includes accessible Appendices A–H. The substantial revision supports reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original post-training loss curves, fitted scaling laws and model-size extrapolation experiments on pruned Llama-3 and Qwen-2.5 models.

after.justification: V2 retains original post-training experiments and reports additional parameterization comparisons, generalization evaluations and embedding-channel analyses, including appendix results.

M1.justification: The selected law retains its multiplicative structure but replaces post-pruning N with pre-pruning N0 inside the additive model-size term (v1 Equation 6; v2 Equation 10). This changes the predictor's pruning dependence. The pruning procedures and sparsity-preserving post-training updates remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use SlimPajama and the same six Llama-3/Qwen-2.5 models under depth, width and 2:4 pruning. V2's generalization experiments reuse this coverage through different fitting and validation arrangements; they introduce no new corpus, domain or downstream task.

E2.justification: V1 evaluates its proposed law without fitted alternative-law comparators. V2 compares L1 against the reduced parameterizations L2 and L3 in Table 2 and adds the OpenAI/Kaplan-based alternatives L4 and L5 in Appendix D, Table 4.

E3.justification: V2 adds all-checkpoint candidate comparisons and R2, Huber-loss and ASD evaluation, sampling ASD from the latter half of training. It introduces lower-to-higher pruning-rate holdouts and excludes Llama-3.1-8B width pruning from all generalization tests, whereas v1 excluded it only from model-size extrapolation. The original training budgets, model sizes and 80/20 checkpoint split are retained.

E4.justification: V2 adds component-removal comparisons through L2/L3, normalized-loss analysis supporting pruning-rate power-law behavior, and higher-pruning-rate generalization tests. Appendix G and Figure 19 investigate the existing Llama-3.1-8B width-pruning anomaly through channel-importance distributions. V1 already identified that anomaly and tested model-size extrapolation.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. V2's added R2, Huber loss and ASD measure prediction fit rather than sampling uncertainty.

E6.justification: V2 adds quantitative parameterization and generalization results in Tables 2–4 and revises fitted coefficients and prediction curves. Table 3 newly reports depth-pruning model-size generalization R2 values of -0.5441 for Llama-3 and -0.8786 for Qwen-2.5. Changed laws and fitting arrangements prevent treating these additions as same-setting performance gains over v1.

T1.justification: V2 adds formal relative-loss definitions, derivative-based necessary conditions, alternative mathematical parameterizations and the new ASD definition (Sections 3–4 and Appendix D). These substantially extend v1's intuitive justification. Table 5 also introduces an apparent sign inconsistency: its positive Llama depth-pruning gamma conflicts with the inverse-rate formula and stated zero-pruning limit.

C1.justification: V1 foregrounds two data-recovery observations and extrapolation from smaller to larger models. V2 adds Average Slope Difference, also called ADS, as an explicit contribution and broadens its headline generalization claims to dataset sizes and pruning rates. It also explicitly claims the first scaling law for post-training after pruning.

C2.justification: V2 retains slope-based extrapolation reasoning but explicitly acknowledges poor absolute-loss generalization to larger models. It removes v1's interpretation that similar fitted width laws imply similar redundancy across model families. Appendix G adds a possible channel-score explanation for the width-pruning failure, and the new Limitation section qualifies applicability to architectures such as MoE.

D1.justification: V2 discloses Levenberg–Marquardt fitting, full-parameter post-training, four GPUs of each stated type and 500 total training hours. Appendix A adds licensing information and a conditional future data-release commitment. Conversely, the explicit billion/million units accompanying v1's fitted formulas are not repeated alongside v2's parameter table.

R1.justification: V2 adds D-CPT and references for fitting and evaluation, including Fisher, Huber and Moré, while removing the LoRA, LLM Surgeon and SlimPajama references. The main pruning literature remains, with more explicit first-law positioning and an empirical justification for choosing Chinchilla-based over OpenAI-based parameterizations.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion are extensively rewritten around P2 Law. Related work moves from Section 2 to Section 5, detailed pruning descriptions move to Appendix B, and the main narrative is reorganized around necessary conditions, parameterization selection and three forms of generalization.

P2.justification: V2 replaces crowded combined fitting displays with separate model-specific plots, relocates many retained loss curves to appendices, and extensively revises legends, axes and captions. It adds normalized-loss and ASD illustrations, channel-importance histograms, and quantitative comparison, generalization and parameter tables.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens v1's mainly visual validation through explicit alternative-law comparisons, quantitative held-out evaluations and investigation of the known width-pruning failure. These address important weaknesses in the justification and assessment of the scaling law. The apparent gamma-sign error in Table 5 harms reproducibility, and larger-model generalization still rests on slope agreement despite poor absolute fit, but these limitations do not outweigh the substantial gains in empirical support and transparency.
